title: Who Holds Oklahoma's Career Rushing Touchdown Record?
question: Who has the most career rushing touchdowns in Oklahoma Sooners history?
answer: Steve Owens holds the Oklahoma career record with 57 rushing touchdowns from 1967 to 1969. Billy Sims is second with 53, and DeMarco Murray is third with 50.
summary: Steve Owens' 57 rushing touchdowns from 1967-69 still top Oklahoma's career list, ahead of Billy Sims, DeMarco Murray and Samaje Perine.
body: Oklahoma has had no shortage of great runners, but when it comes to scoring on the ground, one name sits alone at the top. Steve Owens, who played for the Sooners from 1967 through 1969, finished his career with 57 rushing touchdowns, the most in program history according to the school's own football records supplement and the SoonerStats record book.

Billy Sims, who played from 1975 to 1979, is second with 53. DeMarco Murray (2007 to 2010) is third with 50, followed by Samaje Perine (2014 to 2016) with 49 and Quentin Griffin (1999 to 2002) with 44. Owens reached his total in only three varsity seasons, which makes the gap even more striking.
The single-season mark tells a similar story. Owens ran for 23 touchdowns in 1969, and Sims matched that number in 1979. The two backs share the Oklahoma record, with Sims also scoring 22 in 1978.

Owens earned the 1969 Heisman Trophy that season, when he led the nation with 1,523 rushing yards, and he also holds a famous workload record: 55 carries in a single game against Oklahoma State. The touchdown mark may be less famous than the Heisman, but it has stood up through more than five decades of Sooner backfields, including the wishbone years, Adrian Peterson, and the modern spread offenses.
